title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Giving Full Play to the Judicial Function to Effectively Maintain the Stability of Enterprises and Society
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Fully Exercising the Adjudicative Functions to Effectively Maintain Enterprise and Social Stability

Fa [2002] No. 132

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In the recent period, incidents of enterprise employees gathering and petitioning in groups have occurred continuously in some localities, seriously affecting the normal production and operation order of the enterprises and local social stability. With the deepening of the reform of state-owned enterprises and the adjustment of the economic structure, deep-seated contradictions in the enterprise system and conflicts of interest within enterprises have become more acute, and various contradictions and disputes arising therefrom will further increase. It is noteworthy that conflicts of interest within enterprises are increasingly reflected in various types of litigation in the adjudicative work of the People's Courts. The cases adjudicated and enforced by the People's Courts involving enterprises are also widely concerned by the public, and improper handling may easily trigger mass incidents. Fully exercising the adjudicative functions, properly handling various contradictions and disputes involving enterprises, maintaining the normal production and operation order of enterprises and the legitimate rights and interests of the majority of employees, and preserving the stability of enterprises and society are important tasks for the adjudicative work of the People's Courts at present and for a period to come. Accordingly, the notice is hereby given as follows:

I. Further Strengthen the Awareness of the Overall Situation and Give Full Play to the Role of Adjudicative Work in Maintaining Enterprise and Social Stability

In the socialist market economic system, enterprises are the main market entities. Only when enterprises are invigorated can the market be invigorated; only when enterprises develop can the economy develop; only when enterprises are stable can society be stable. The reform of state-owned enterprises is the central link in establishing the socialist market economic system. Currently, the reform of state-owned enterprises is in a critical stage. With the acceleration of the reorganization and transformation of state-owned enterprises and the intensification of the adjustment of ownership structure and industrial structure, the number of laid-off workers has increased significantly. Coupled with the imperfection of the social security system, some deep-seated contradictions within state-owned enterprises have gradually emerged, and conflicts of interest have become acute, showing the characteristics of prominent contradictions and increased disputes. At the same time, many new situations and problems have also emerged in the rapid development of non-state-owned enterprises. In particular, some foreign-invested enterprises, private enterprises, and individual economic organizations violate labor, safety, and social insurance laws and regulations, infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of employees to a large extent, and some are quite serious. Mass, sudden, and vicious incidents caused by labor disputes occur frequently. If these problems cannot be properly resolved in a timely manner, they will not only seriously interfere with the internal reform and production operation of enterprises but also adversely affect the overall situation of the country's reform, development, and stability. The People's Courts are the judicial organs of the state and play an irreplaceable and important role in ensuring the reform of state-owned enterprises and maintaining enterprise stability. Courts at all levels must, from the height of adhering to Deng Xiaoping Theory and practicing Comrade Jiang Zemin's requirement of the "Three Represents," deeply understand the significance of ensuring the reform of state-owned enterprises and maintaining enterprise stability, further strengthen the awareness of the overall situation, the sense of responsibility, and the sense of safeguarding, promptly and impartially adjudicate various types of cases related to enterprise reform, development, and stability in accordance with the law, and give full play to the normative, guiding, regulating, and safeguarding roles of the law with respect to the various interests involved in enterprise reform. They must both vigorously ensure the internal reform of enterprises and effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of employees, ensuring that adjudicated cases achieve good legal and social effects. While strictly handling cases according to law, attention must be paid to doing a good job in all aspects to prevent the intensification of contradictions or the expansion of incidents during the adjudication process. Particularly for mass disputes, ideological attention must be high, and work must be meticulously organized. Through case adjudication, contradictions should be resolved, relationships straightened out, people's minds calmed, and order maintained, providing strong judicial guarantees and services for reform, development, and stability.

II. Continue to Deeply Carry Out the Campaign to Crack Down on Serious Crimes, Creating a Good Public Security Environment for Enterprises

Creating and maintaining a long-term stable public security environment is of great significance for ensuring the reform of state-owned enterprises and the development of various types of enterprises. Since the launch of the campaign to crack down on serious crimes, the upward trend of criminal cases has been curbed to a certain extent, but the public security situation remains severe. Courts at all levels must continue to actively and effectively carry out the crackdown campaign in depth, and pay close attention to the adjudication of major criminal cases. For criminal cases where domestic and foreign hostile forces, terrorist forces, religious extremists, separatists, and cult organizations such as "Falun Gong" take advantage of difficulties and unstable factors in enterprises to carry out sabotage and disruption; criminal cases of organized crime of a mafia nature and hooligan evil forces that severely disturb enterprise security and production operation order; criminal cases where, due to dissatisfaction with the reform of state-owned enterprises, violent means are used to retaliate against society, killing enterprise managers and employees; and criminal cases of looting, stealing enterprise property, and destroying or intentionally damaging enterprise means of production, equipment, etc., trials must be expedited and conducted in a timely manner, and criminals must be severely punished according to the law with heavy penalties and swift justice.

III. Continue to Severely Punish Various Economic Crimes to Safeguard the Socialist Market Economic Order

Courts at all levels must continue to actively participate in the work of rectifying and standardizing the order of the market economy, and severely crack down according to law on various serious crimes that undermine the order of the socialist market economy. For criminal activities that infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises, such as producing and selling counterfeit and shoddy goods, infringing upon trademark rights, patent rights, copyrights, and trade secrets, damaging commercial credit and commodity reputation, bid rigging, contract fraud; and criminal activities that undermine the order of the market economy, such as smuggling, falsely issuing special VAT invoices, tax evasion and tax resistance, financial fraud, illegal business operations, etc., such activities must be severely punished according to law to protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises and market management order. At the same time, for crimes involving enterprises and their personnel, such as falsely reporting or withdrawing registered capital, illegally absorbing public deposits, issuing or fraudulently issuing stocks or bonds without authorization, insider trading, fabricating or disseminating false information, providing false financial reports and certification documents, manipulating trading prices, disrupting the securities market, and seriously harming the interests of shareholders and investors, such crimes must also be resolutely and severely punished according to law.

IV. Continue to Severely Punish Various Corruption Crimes According to Law to Protect State-Owned Assets and the Interests of Enterprise Employees

Hearing cases of corruption crimes that occur in party and government leading organs, administrative law enforcement organs, judicial organs, and economic management departments, as well as among leading cadres at the county and department level or above and leading personnel of state-owned enterprises, is the focus of the current anti-corruption struggle and a requirement for maintaining enterprise stability. For criminal cases occurring in state-owned enterprises, such as embezzlement, bribery, misappropriation of public funds, illegal distribution of state-owned assets, illegal operation of similar businesses, and illegally seeking profits for relatives and friends, especially criminal cases of embezzling, illegally distributing, or misappropriating state-owned assets by taking advantage of the reorganization, merger, leasing, contracting, and shareholding reform of state-owned enterprises; duty crimes of embezzling, misappropriating, or collectively distributing various social security funds; and criminal cases of accepting bribes, engaging in malpractice for personal gain, intentionally undervaluing state-owned assets during enterprise mergers and acquisitions involving changes in property rights, resulting in the loss of state-owned assets, such crimes must be resolutely and severely punished according to law. For state functionaries who take advantage of their positions to solicit or accept property from non-state-owned enterprises, they must also be severely punished according to law. The anti-corruption struggle must be closely integrated with the ongoing campaigns to crack down on serious crimes, rectify and standardize the market economy. For those who act as "backstage bosses" and "protective umbrellas" for various criminal activities, and for corrupt and derelict criminals who are responsible for major liability accidents, major labor safety accidents, and major engineering safety accidents, they must be resolutely and severely punished according to law.

V. Conduct Civil, Commercial, Administrative Adjudication and Enforcement Work Well to Create a Good Legal Environment for Enterprise Reform and Development

Cases of disputes arising from enterprise reorganization, merger, leasing, contracting, and equity participation must be adjudicated according to law to ensure the smooth completion of the strategic reorganization of state-owned enterprises. For cases involving the merger, bankruptcy, and closure of large and medium-sized state-owned enterprises, they must be handled properly in strict accordance with relevant laws, regulations, rules, policies, and judicial interpretations. For cases of enterprise mergers and acquisitions and other asset restructurings involving changes in property rights, asset evaluation must be strictly regulated according to law, to prevent both the loss of state-owned assets and the evasion of bank debts and state taxes, while also promoting enterprise capital increase, debt reduction, and asset restructuring. Dispute cases arising from the establishment and improvement of the modern enterprise system by state-owned enterprises must be adjudicated according to law to protect the enterprise's operational autonomy and the state's management of state-owned assets. Cases involving state-owned enterprise equity, creditor's rights, debts, etc., must be adjudicated according to law to ensure and promote the enhancement of enterprises' direct investment and financing, and to maintain the controlling power of the state-owned economy and the legitimate rights and interests of banks and other creditors. Labor dispute cases must be handled promptly and properly according to law to protect the legitimate rights and interests of workers, promote the reform of the labor system, and support enterprises in strengthening and improving management. Adjudicative means must be used to promptly and impartially resolve disputes arising in the economic exchanges of enterprises, protect enterprises that engage in fair competition and lawful operations, and maintain market economic order and transaction security. Administrative cases involving state-owned enterprises must be adjudicated according to law, resolutely stopping all kinds of arbitrary charges, fines, apportionments, and other acts harmful to the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises, while supporting state administrative organs in exercising their powers according to law. For cases involving key projects and key construction projects of large and medium-sized state-owned enterprises with large amounts in dispute and significant impact on production development, cases must be filed and tried quickly, and concluded in a timely manner. Courts at all levels must adjudicate civil and commercial cases affecting enterprise stability in a timely manner according to law. In particular, illegal acts of evading debts by taking advantage of enterprise restructuring must be severely sanctioned according to law to protect the legitimate rights and interests of injured enterprises.

Courts at all levels shall uphold specific administrative acts made by administrative organs according to law in the process of rectifying and standardizing market order. For specific administrative acts that are illegally made by administrative organs and infringe upon the operational autonomy of enterprises, the People's Courts shall render judgments to revoke them. For administrative organs that fail to perform their statutory duties, resulting in the failure to protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises, the People's Courts shall render judgments requiring the administrative organs to perform their statutory duties according to law.

Enforcement work involving the interests of enterprises, especially those in difficulty, must be well-handled to eliminate unstable factors arising from inadequate enforcement. The issue of enterprise debt enforcement must be effectively resolved, local protectionism overcome, and effective measures taken to solve the problem of out-of-area enforcement. The enforcing court must pay attention to preventing both unstable social factors arising from inadequate enforcement and unstable social factors arising from disorderly enforcement. For enforcement cases involving enterprise stability, on the premise of law enforcement, attention must be paid to enforcement skills and methods, and the unity of legal and social effects of enforcement work.

VI. Do a Good Job in Receiving Petitioners, Properly Handle Group Petition Incidents

Courts at all levels must attach great importance to the issue of contradictions among the people under the new situation, and regard the proper handling of contradictions among the people as a political task to maintain enterprise stability, and earnestly grasp and implement it. The task of handling letters and visits must be placed in a position equally important as adjudicative work, and the work of receiving letters and visits from the masses must be carefully done to resolve contradictions in a timely manner. For petitioners, especially group petitioners among laid-off workers of enterprises, patient education and guidance must be carried out, their difficulties must be seriously understood, and practical problems must be actively helped to solve to prevent the intensification of contradictions. Channels should be broadened, horizontal connections strengthened, and for difficult petition cases, initiative must be taken to contact relevant departments to provide opinions for consultation and joint handling. It is necessary to correctly guide and protect the rights of petitioners according to law, pay attention to persuading the parties to accept the judgment and abide by the law, strengthen legal publicity and persuasion education, and promptly neutralize the confrontational emotions of the parties. For cases where the judgment is indeed erroneous, cases must be promptly filed for review, errors corrected in accordance with statutory procedures, and the legitimate rights and interests of the parties protected. For cases where the original judgment is correct but the parties persistently petition without grounds for appeal, effective measures must be taken to resolve the matter with the support of relevant departments, to maintain the normal work order of the People's Courts.

VII. Combine Adjudicative Work, Actively Participate in Comprehensive Management to Maintain Enterprise and Social Stability

Courts at all levels must continuously summarize the experience of adjudicating cases involving the interests of a large number of enterprise employees, and provide suggestions to local relevant departments on maintaining enterprise stability in the form of judicial suggestions, etc. They should combine typical cases of protecting legitimate enterprises and the legitimate rights and interests of enterprise employees, adopt various forms to vigorously promote the law, uphold the authority of the Party, the government, and the judiciary, and continuously improve the awareness and ability of the masses to use legal means to protect their legitimate rights and interests.

VIII. Strengthen Leadership, Clarify Responsibilities, and Ensure the Implementation of Maintaining Enterprise and Social Stability

This year is the first year of China's accession to the World Trade Organization, and the Sixteenth National Congress of the Communist Party of China is about to be convened. Doing a good job in all adjudicative work and effectively maintaining enterprise and social stability is of particular significance. Leaders of courts at all levels must earnestly strengthen leadership over the work of maintaining stability. On the basis of the existing leading group for maintaining stability, combined with the division of adjudicative business, a capable working organ should be established, various systems improved, the scope of responsibilities clarified, and implementation work done well. It is necessary to periodically analyze the situation in conjunction with adjudicative work and local realities, identify problems and cases that affect or may affect enterprise and social stability, formulate practical countermeasures and measures, and ensure they are implemented in place to achieve practical results. Courts at all levels must adhere to the system of timely reporting major matters level by level. When signs and information affecting enterprise and social stability are discovered, they must immediately report to the local Party committee and reflect to relevant departments. For incidents affecting stability that occur or are discovered in the course of adjudicative work, while quickly taking control measures, they must be promptly reported level by level, and must not be delayed or concealed. Special attention must be paid to preventing major incidents affecting enterprise and social stability due to errors in adjudicative work.

Upon receipt of this notice, courts at all levels shall, in light of local realities, promptly formulate implementation measures and report the implementation status in writing to this Court.

June 21, 2002
